source: FT-891 CAT Operation Reference Book, 1909-C; every command tried on a real FT-891 over CAT at 38400 baud

commands.name: Transmit
commands.note: 0 receive; 1 transmitting on CAT's command; 2 transmitting on the radio's own PTT or MOX (answer only).

commands.name: Band select
commands.note: Band stack numbers of the FT-891 CAT reference: 00 1.8 MHz to 10 50 MHz, 11 GEN, 12 MW; 02 is not used, so 60 m has no band-stack key.

commands.name: VFO-A to memory
commands.confirm: Overwrite the current memory channel with VFO-A?

commands.name: Power switch
commands.note: Switching on needs a wake-up: the server sends PS1; twice, one second apart.
commands.confirm: Switch the radio off? It can only be switched back on over CAT if its USB port stays powered.

commands.name: Auto information
commands.note: Kept off by the server, which reads the radio on its own schedule.

commands.name: SPL — split
commands.note: Switched with ST (0 off, 1 on); read through RI (SPLIT indicator).

commands.name: QS — quick split
commands.note: VFO-B takes the frequency of VFO-A moved by menu 05-13 QUICK SPL FREQ, and split is switched on.

commands.name: SFT — IF shift
commands.note: IF shift on/off, then the offset: IS01+0500; turns the shift on at +500 Hz.

commands.name: WDH — width
commands.note: Width on: the step applies; off: the mode's default width. The steps, and the bandwidth each one gives, depend on the mode and on NARROW: SSB 09-21 (01-09 narrow), CW, RTTY and DATA 10-17 (01-10 narrow); none in AM and FM.

commands.name: AGC
commands.note: Set to AUTO, the radio answers AUTO-FAST (shown as AUTO), AUTO-MID or AUTO-SLOW, depending on the mode.

commands.name: BK-IN — delay
commands.note: BREAK-IN delay, 30 to 3000 ms in 10 ms steps (menu 07-09 CW BK-IN DELAY).

commands.name: Keyer memory 1 — text
commands.note: Played as typed only when menu 04-07 CW MEMORY 1 is set to TEXT.

commands.name: Keyer memory 2 — text
commands.note: Played as typed only when menu 04-08 CW MEMORY 2 is set to TEXT.

commands.name: Keyer memory 3 — text
commands.note: Played as typed only when menu 04-09 CW MEMORY 3 is set to TEXT.

commands.name: Keyer memory 4 — text
commands.note: Played as typed only when menu 04-10 CW MEMORY 4 is set to TEXT.

commands.name: Keyer memory 5 — text
commands.note: Played as typed only when menu 04-11 CW MEMORY 5 is set to TEXT.

commands.name: Keyer memory 1 — play (TEXT)
commands.note: Plays the text of keyer memory 1 (written with KM1), for a memory set to TEXT in menu 04-07. On the FT-891 a TEXT memory is played by KY6-KYA; KY1-KY5 are refused ("?").

commands.name: Keyer memory 2 — play (TEXT)
commands.note: Plays the text of keyer memory 2 (written with KM2), for a memory set to TEXT in menu 04-08. On the FT-891 a TEXT memory is played by KY6-KYA; KY1-KY5 are refused ("?").

commands.name: Keyer memory 3 — play (TEXT)
commands.note: Plays the text of keyer memory 3 (written with KM3), for a memory set to TEXT in menu 04-09. On the FT-891 a TEXT memory is played by KY6-KYA; KY1-KY5 are refused ("?").

commands.name: Keyer memory 4 — play (TEXT)
commands.note: Plays the text of keyer memory 4 (written with KM4), for a memory set to TEXT in menu 04-10. On the FT-891 a TEXT memory is played by KY6-KYA; KY1-KY5 are refused ("?").

commands.name: Keyer memory 5 — play (TEXT)
commands.note: Plays the text of keyer memory 5 (written with KM5), for a memory set to TEXT in menu 04-11. On the FT-891 a TEXT memory is played by KY6-KYA; KY1-KY5 are refused ("?").

commands.name: Keyer memory 1 — play (MESSAGE)
commands.note: Plays the message recorded with the paddle, for memory 1 set to MESSAGE in menu 04-07.

commands.name: Keyer memory 2 — play (MESSAGE)
commands.note: Plays the message recorded with the paddle, for memory 2 set to MESSAGE in menu 04-08.

commands.name: Keyer memory 3 — play (MESSAGE)
commands.note: Plays the message recorded with the paddle, for memory 3 set to MESSAGE in menu 04-09.

commands.name: Keyer memory 4 — play (MESSAGE)
commands.note: Plays the message recorded with the paddle, for memory 4 set to MESSAGE in menu 04-10.

commands.name: Keyer memory 5 — play (MESSAGE)
commands.note: Plays the message recorded with the paddle, for memory 5 set to MESSAGE in menu 04-11.

commands.name: RPT — repeater shift
commands.note: Only accepted in FM.

commands.name: RF gain
commands.note: 0 to 30, as the radio takes it; the CAT reference gives 000-100.

commands.name: Identification
commands.note: Answers 0650 on an FT-891, as the CAT reference prints it. Hamlib expects 135 instead and keys its repeater-shift table on that value, so one of the two is wrong; a single ID; on the radio settles it.

commands.name: 04-04 BEACON INTERVAL
commands.note: 000 switches the beacon off. A non-zero value makes a played memory repeat.

commands.name: 05-06 CAT RATE
commands.note: Changing this breaks the link until the server is set to match.
commands.confirm: Change the CAT rate? The link stops until the server is set to the same speed.

commands.name: 07-12 PC KEYING
commands.note: Selects the line that keys CW from the computer.

commands.name: 09-05 RPT SHIFT 50MHz
commands.note: The manual's table says one digit here; four is what the range needs, and what the 28 MHz entry uses.

commands.name: 11-05 SSB MIC SELECT
commands.note: REAR feeds the rig from the rear socket and mutes the front microphone.

commands.name: 17-01 RESET
commands.note: Resets the radio. There is no confirmation and no undo. It is an action, not a setting: the radio has nothing to answer when asked, so it is left out of the bulk read.
commands.confirm: Reset the radio? There is no undo.
